description: Pipeline hygiene finding, not a dome-site change. The operator's mounted dome-model-review workspace folder (used for LOCAL-mode runs and for reading state in CLOUD-mode runs) has a corrupted git ref: 'refs/heads/main.stale-lock-1791850063' is a bad object that makes `git fetch`/`git pull` fail outright in that folder ('fatal: bad object refs/heads/main.stale-lock-1791850063'), and several '.git/objects/**/tmp_obj_*' temp files cannot be unlinked there (Operation not permitted — delete is disabled on this connected folder). The folder was also left 5 polls stale (still at commit f2e56e5b / 2026-10-11T06:11:55Z) because, per execution-mode.md, this and recent cloud-mode poller runs correctly do their actual git work in a fresh $TMPDIR clone rather than the mounted folder, so nothing writes the mounted folder forward. One untracked leftover file, monitor/changes/chg-20261012-0008-001.json, sits in the mounted folder; its content is byte-identical to the already-committed-and-pushed copy at commit 097c0414, so no information was lost. This run did its real git work in a fresh $TMPDIR clone (per C1-C5) and does not touch the mounted folder at all, so the corruption does not block today's poll. Flagging for tinker/decider: the mounted clone will need an operator or LOCAL-mode repair (e.g. remove the stale-lock ref and tmp objects, or re-point/re-clone the folder) before any LOCAL-mode agent run or manual inspection of it can trust its git plumbing again. This is now the second class of mounted-workspace hygiene issue logged this cycle (see the 2026-10-11 workspace-mount-staleness finding in status.json), and both stem from the same root cause: cloud-mode runs since 2026-10-07 never write the mounted clone forward.
before: Mounted workspace at commit f2e56e5b (2026-10-11T06:11:55Z), git fetch untested since.
after: Mounted workspace git fetch confirmed broken (bad ref refs/heads/main.stale-lock-1791850063); 1 harmless untracked duplicate file present; origin/main is current (fff22a6c as of this poll's start). Not fixed by this run -- read-only diagnosis only, no delete permission available and no git write attempted against the mounted folder.
